title: Ticket Prices Rising at Japan's Amusement Parks
paragraphs: Going to a theme park in Japan is becoming more expensive.

Teikoku Databank, a Japanese research company, looked at the prices of 190 popular leisure places in Japan, such as amusement parks, aquariums and zoos. It found that 50 of them, or about 26%, raised their ticket prices in 2026. That is fewer than last year, when 71 places raised their prices.

On average, an entrance ticket now costs 1,768 yen. This is 4.2% more than last year. A "free pass," which lets people enter and also go on all the rides, now costs 5,033 yen on average. This is the first time the average price has been more than 5,000 yen.
Aquariums had the most expensive entrance tickets, at 2,202 yen on average. Amusement parks and theme parks cost 1,728 yen, and zoos cost 1,473 yen.
Why are prices going up? The parks need to pay workers more money, and the cost of electricity has also gone up.
Some popular parks now use "dynamic pricing." This means ticket prices change depending on the day. Prices are higher on busy days, such as during Golden Week and summer vacation.
However, Teikoku Databank warned that raising prices too much could be risky. Many people's salaries are not rising as fast as prices, so some people may stop visiting.
